_comment: Soft regression baselines, keyed BY DEVICE.
They were flat until 2026-08-03, and the first run on a second phone
compared its node cold start (61 ms) against the first phone's recorded
57 ms and printed 'ok'.  That is not a regression check -- byte-identical
code gives 55 ms on one reference device and 61 ms on the other.  A flat
baseline both hides a real regression behind a faster phone and invents a
fake one on a slower one.
The key comes from tests/device/bench.sh:  model/platform/androidNN/K.K
Hard invariants are device-independent and are NOT keyed here.
Reference #1 (MediaTek MT8775 / SM-X236N / Android 16 / kernel 6.1) is
NOT listed, deliberately.  Its numbers are exec_per_sec 341 and
node_cold_ms 57.0, but its ro.board.platform was never recorded and the
phone was not in hand when this file was re-keyed.  Writing a guessed key
would silently never match, so the entry is left for that device's next
run to create -- the gate prints NEW rather than passing on nothing.
